analysis.title: Bitcoin Erases Its Entire "Debasement" Rally As Goldman Says Every August Catalyst Has Reversed
key_insights: BTC fell to a weekend low of roughly $62k and ETH to $1,711, then stabilized near $65k and $1,826 in Monday's Asia session. BTC is down 16% in November and 26% year-to-date.
Goldman's FICC crypto desk says both assets have fully unwound the price inflection that began on 19 August. BTC is back at pre-August levels and ETH is slightly below its August range.

The August rally was triggered by Treasury doubling long-end buybacks on August 19 (30Y yields at 20-year highs), which lifted gold first, then crypto, with support from a White House crypto event urging passage of the CLARITY Act.
Gold unwound first (below its August 19 range by mid-September) and bitcoin has now caught up. Goldman's commodity team recently cut its gold target again.

Goldman says the conditions and catalysts behind the August rally have reversed and in some cases worsened. Hotter-than-expected CPI was the third straight month of bad inflation news, and Goldman economists added a third rate hike to their forecast. Markets price three hikes into early Q2 next year.
Rates and dollar moved against crypto since August: 10Y yield 5.14% vs 4.70%, 30Y 5.47% vs 5.28%, DXY from a 98 handle to a 103 handle.

The Senate blocked the CLARITY Act in September. House Democrats are drafting their own market structure bill with a bigger SEC role. Goldman says regulatory progress continued through agency channels but legislative momentum did not materialize.

US spot BTC ETFs lost $1B last week, taking year-to-date net flows to -$1.9B. US spot ETH ETFs lost $398M last week, taking year-to-date flows to -$804M. Goldman says outflows accelerated through November.
ETH's realized price was $2,213 at the start of November. At $1,826 the average ETH holder is about 17% underwater.

BTC lost its 200-day moving average on 12 November and its 200-week moving average (about $68k) on 14 November. Thin weekend liquidity produced forced selling, with $1.78B of BTC liquidations across 13-15 November.
Perpetual futures funding fell back to flat as of Monday, from near 10% annualized earlier. Funding peaks in 2021 and early 2024 were roughly 90-125%, so leverage this time was far less extreme.

BTC 1-month 25-delta risk reversals are at -5.09%, the most bearish of all tenors, so downside protection is better bid than upside. Goldman suggests that those fading the move might fund calls by selling puts.

The article's author argues against selling puts below the 200-week moving average during a hiking cycle, and would wait for ETF flows to return or for the Fed to ease. Today's skew is far from the roughly -37% 1M risk reversal in 2022, which the article reads as fear but not capitulation.
Anthropic's IPO next Thursday may be pulling speculative capital away from crypto, per the article.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 4.70% in August, a headwind for non-yielding assets such as BTC.
Dollar up from a 98 handle in August, tightening financial conditions for crypto.
Third straight month of bad inflation news, which led Goldman economists to add a third rate hike to their forecast.

macro_indicators.reading: Three hikes priced into early Q2 next year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman says a hawkish Fed keeps debasement concerns contained, which removes the narrative that supported gold and BTC in August.

crypto_views: Goldman's FICC crypto desk: BTC and ETH have fully unwound the rally that began on 19 August.
US-listed spot BTC and ETH ETF outflows accelerated through November. BTC ETF cumulative flows are about $57B, down from a peak near $65B in October 2025.
Liquidations of $1.78B across 13-15 November followed the break of the 200-week moving average. Funding has reset to flat.
Legislative momentum for crypto market structure (CLARITY Act) stalled in the Senate. House Democrats are drafting a bill with a bigger SEC role.
ETH is about 17% below its realized price of $2,213.

trade_ideas.description: Fade the BTC move by funding call purchases with put sales (call financed by short put, risk-reversal style)
trade_ideas.rationale: Goldman says funding is flat, longs are flushed, and downside skew is bid, so selling puts pays for calls.
trade_ideas.risk: The article's author says the drivers (Fed hikes, 10Y above 5%, stronger dollar, ETF outflows) remain and selling puts below the 200-week moving average is like picking up pennies in front of a steamroller.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman notes funding is flat and longs are flushed, leaving room for a squeeze, and skew pays sellers of puts to wait. Leverage was also well below the 2021 and early-2024 extremes.
tension_points.bear_case: The drivers of the unwind remain: the Fed is hiking into December, the 10Y is above 5%, the dollar is rising, ETF holders are leaving, and the Anthropic IPO may pull speculative capital. Skew at -5% is far from the 2022 panic level, so this is fear but not yet capitulation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ETF inflows returning or the Fed pausing or easing would undermine the bear case. For the bull case, the article says selling puts below the 200-week moving average (about $68k) in a hiking cycle is risky.
